adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Anonymous-reachable 500: negative `limit`/`offset` params are passed straight to SQL (`LIMIT -1` / `OFFSET -1` are rejected by Postgres).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination params are taken directly from request params (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, `offset = params[:offset].to_i`) and passed to ActiveRecord (`.limit(limit).offset(offset)`) with no non-negative validation/clamping. A negative `offset` (e.g. `-1`) will be sent to Postgres as `OFFSET -1`, which Postgres rejects, producing a 500 on an anonymous-reachable endpoint. This exposure is widened by the diff because pagination now applies to all groups, not just `automatic?` groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` has no maximum, so `?limit=99999999` on a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0) dumps every member in one anonymous request.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound. This means a request like `?limit=99999999` can force an extremely large query/response for large groups (automatic or otherwise), a performance/DoS risk introduced/exposed by the change to accept `limit` for all groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unknown/misspelled usernames are silently skipped yet the endpoint still returns success_json, so the admin UI reports a successful add that added nobody.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are ignored (`if user = ...`). It then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if no users were added. This matches the finding that invalid/misspelled usernames are silently skipped while the endpoint still reports success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — The add loop is not wrapped in a transaction and `group.add` persists per-user, so an exception or validation failure midway leaves a partially-updated membership with an error response.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are iterated and `group.add(user)` is called for each (`usernames.split(",").each do ... group.add(user) ... end`), with no surrounding transaction. If `group.add` writes membership immediately (common for join-table inserts) and a later exception or the final `group.save` fails, earlier additions would not be rolled back, leading to a partially-updated group despite an error path. The diff shows the lack of transaction, but it does not prove `group.add` persists per-user or that `group.save` can fail in practice, so it’s a grounded robustness concern rather than a definitively verifiable bug from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id)` resolves ids via `find`, so removing an already-removed member (double-click, two admins, stale page) raises RecordNotFound -> 404 instead of the previous idempotent success.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff changes removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` (with `user_id` coming from params) and does not handle the case where the user is no longer in the association. In Rails, calling `delete` on a collection association with an id commonly goes through an association-scoped `find` (i.e., `group.users.find(user_id)`), which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the record is not currently associated. That makes repeated removals (double-click/stale UI/two admins) potentially non-idempotent and able to error instead of succeeding as a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:77 — group.save` is used as the success signal but the membership mutation already persisted independently, so a failing group validation returns 422 after the change took effect.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member, membership changes are applied via association mutations (group.add(user) and group.users.delete(user_id)) before checking group.save for success. In Rails, deleting/adding through associations typically persists immediately to the join table, while group.save only validates/saves the Group record. If group.save fails (e.g., due to validations/callbacks on Group), the controller returns a 422 even though the membership change already took effect, leaving the client with an error response for a successful mutation. This risk is directly visible in the diff: the mutation happens before the conditional on group.save in both actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40 — Removing the last member of the last page leaves `offset` past the new total, so the list silently renders empty until the admin pages back.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the request offset is clamped using the *current* `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`) before the AJAX call updates `user_count` from `result.meta.total`. After deleting the last member on the last page, `removeMember` calls `self.findMembers()` while `user_count` is still the old total, so it can request an offset that is now equal to (or beyond) the new total (e.g. total drops from 51 to 50 while offset stays 50). The server then returns an empty `members` array with `meta.total` smaller, and the UI renders empty until the admin clicks "previous" to reduce offset. This behavior is directly implied by `removeMember` -> `findMembers` and the offset calculation/update in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Usernames are not stripped and the list length is uncapped: one request with thousands of comma-separated names does one `find_by_username` plus insert each, serially.

This means inputs like "bob, alice" will attempt to look up " alice" (leading space) and fail to add intended users, and a very long comma-separated list will trigger many sequential `find_by_username` calls and adds in one request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — visible` is still assigned unconditionally from params, so any legacy PUT that sends `group[visible]=true` (or omits the new flat key) silently flips the group to not-visible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, so an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50) reports one phantom extra page that renders empty and keeps "next" enabled

For an exact multiple (e.g. user_count=50, limit=50) this yields 2 pages although only one page of results exists. The "next" action then sets offset to Math.min(offset+limit, user_count) (0->50) and Group.findMembers requests offset=50, producing an empty members list from /groups/:name/members.json. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, offset), so an offset equal to user_count is sent verbatim and returns an empty page instead of the last populated page

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33 — next clamps the new offset to user_count rather than to the start of the last page, so it can land mid-page/past the end

adjudication.rationale: In `actions.next`, the new offset is computed as `Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`. If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 with limit 50), this sets `offset` to `user_count` (100), which is past the last valid page start (should be 50). `findMembers` then sends that offset to `/groups/.../members.json`, and the backend applies `offset` directly, yielding an empty page. This is a real paging correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40 — removeMember/addMembers never propagate failures: the returned promise has no rejection handler in the controller, so a 422 (automatic group) or 404 (non-member) silently does nothing in the UI

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — limit/offset are taken unvalidated from params: a negative offset produces an invalid SQL OFFSET (500) and a non-numeric limit becomes 0, which also makes the client's page math divide by zero

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. This allows `offset` to be negative (e.g. "-10" -> -10), which can produce an invalid SQL `OFFSET -10` and error. It also allows a non-numeric `limit` to become `0` (e.g. "abc".to_i -> 0), and the client computes `currentPage`/`totalPages` by dividing by `limit` in `admin-group.js.es6` (`Math.floor(user_count / limit)` and `Math.floor(offset / limit)`), which will break (division by zero/infinite pages) if the server returns `meta.limit: 0`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) on the has_many :through, deleting join rows directly and bypassing Group#remove plus GroupUser callbacks/user_count counter cache, leaving user_count stale

The diff itself doesn’t prove `user_count` will become stale, but it does show an inconsistent removal mechanism that could skip model-layer behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — passing an id to collection.delete resolves it via find, so removing a user who is not a member now raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding silently as the removed PATCH path did

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff changes member removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` (passing an integer id). On an association (`group.users`), `delete(id)` is resolved via an association lookup; if the user_id is not currently in that association scope (i.e., not a member), Rails can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` rather than no-op. The prior PATCH-based path removed members by first `find_by_username` and then calling `group.remove(user)`, which would silently do nothing if the user wasn’t in the group. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — unknown or whitespace-padded usernames are silently skipped yet the endpoint still returns success_json, so the UI reports success for members that were never added

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — concurrent findMembers calls (rapid next/previous) are not sequenced, so a late response can overwrite offset/members with a stale page
